statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band well below the block threshold, while Stress stays elevated on the oil-led inflation impulse, a 4.76 percent 10-year yield and hawkish September rate repricing.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with a contained, two-sided regime in which mean reversion is functioning: the Nasdaq-100 has traded a full round trip inside its session range and sits mid-range rather than at an extreme into the month-end close. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the S&P Global Manufacturing PMI, ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS releases on 1 September between 13:45 and 15:00 UTC, where conditional Tail peaks in the watch band. The August month-end cash close at 20:00 UTC today is a secondary checkpoint. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this descriptive assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds mid-range into the month-end close as Brent above 90 dollars and a 4.76 percent 10-year keep Stress elevated
body: The Nasdaq-100 is near 29,377, down about 0.19 percent, after traversing its full 29,304 to 29,465 session range in both directions and settling in the middle of it with roughly half an hour to the August month-end cash close. That round trip remains the central price-path observation: retracements are deep, pullbacks are not unusually shallow, and the index is not pinned to a session extreme. VIX is 15.01, up about 4 percent on the day but already back off its 15.48 high and low in absolute terms. Breadth is soft, with the S&P 500 down about 0.40 percent and the Dow about 0.63 percent, so the Nasdaq is outperforming a weaker tape while energy leads. Three channels dominate. First, the renewed Strait of Hormuz escalation after US strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island and Iranian retaliation against facilities in Jordan has lifted WTI about 2.8 percent to roughly 85.70 dollars, with Brent above 90 dollars, against a Hormuz crisis in which transit traffic is already down about 95 percent. Second, that energy impulse is feeding a hawkish rate repricing: the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.758 percent, up about 4 basis points and its highest intraday level since January 2025, the 30-year is up 5 basis points to 5.26 percent while the 2-year is broadly unchanged near 4.35 percent, and market-implied odds of a September rate hike have risen to roughly 62 percent from about 40 percent a week ago after Chairman Warsh's 28 August Jackson Hole remarks framed inflation as still above target. Bear steepening of this kind widens the distribution of outcomes, which is why Stress is elevated. Third, index-level dispersion has increased on company news rather than on macro: Amazon is down about 3 percent after reports that the FTC and more than 20 state attorneys general are suing it over advertising auction pricing, while Nvidia is up about 1 percent on its 3.5 billion dollar convertible investment in MediaTek and Tesla is higher on Hong Kong and Macau price cuts. Offsetting single-name moves of this kind raise dispersion and Stress without producing the index-level directional efficiency that Tail measures, so Tail stays low. The identified checkpoints are the August month-end cash close at 20:00 UTC today, where rebalancing imbalances can impose a short directional drift, and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases at 14:00 UTC on 1 September, which carry the clearest mechanism for a repricing leg that could deny retracement.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours cover the late Sunday Globex reopen through the US Monday afternoon session. Tail began at 5 with a quiet, orderly regime, rose to 15 around the 00:00 UTC Asian reprice of the Larak Island strikes, eased back to 5 through the European morning, and spiked briefly to 17 at 09:00 UTC on the crude-led inflation impulse before settling between 9 and 13 through the US session. Stress climbed from 30 to 55 as oil, long-end yields and September rate-hike odds all repriced hawkishly. The action mapping stayed EA_ON and green for all 24 hours, because at no point did the assessed price path show the persistent no-retracement structure that raises Tail. Confidence held in the 84 to 88 band throughout on continuously available live price and cross-asset evidence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours run from the US Monday afternoon through the month-end cash close, the Globex maintenance break, the Asian and European sessions, and into the Tuesday US afternoon. Conditional Tail eases to 7 during the 21:00 UTC maintenance halt when no price path can form, drifts between 10 and 12 overnight, firms to 13 in the mid-European morning, and peaks at 22 in the 14:00 UTC hour on 1 September when ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS Job Openings release simultaneously into an already hawkish rate backdrop. That is the only hour mapped to WATCH and yellow; every other hour remains EA_ON and green. The danger window is deliberately narrow at 13:45 to 15:00 UTC, covering the S&P Global PMI final, the double release and the immediate yield-reaction leg. Stress peaks at 64 in the same hour and decays afterwards on the assumption of orderly price discovery. Confidence decays from 88 to 61 with distance from the last live observation, which is the expected horizon effect rather than an evidence problem.

forecast.analysis: The CME equity-index maintenance halt runs through this hour, so no continuous price path can form and mean-reversion failure is mechanically close to impossible. Conditional Tail is at its 24-hour low. Stress falls with it, although the oil and long-end yield backdrop carried into the break is unchanged.

forecast.analysis: Globex reopens for the 1 September session during this hour. The reopen is the first chance for headlines accumulated in the halt to price, so a gap and a fast first leg are plausible; a reopen gap that then retraces would be normal and would not by itself indicate a no-retracement path.
drivers: Globex reopen: first repricing window for headlines accumulated during the halt
Reopen gaps are a checkpoint, not evidence of persistent one-way structure
Thin post-reopen liquidity widens the short-term range

Tail stays in the low band absent an observed sequence of failed retracements.

No scheduled US macro release falls in this window
